+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+The Security Profiles Operator (SPO) is the Kubernetes ecosystem pilot for this pattern.
+SPO uses Cloud Build with a project-specific staging service account, self-signed SLSA L1 provenance, and a kpromo provenance policy in `require` mode.
+SPO v1.1.2 was the first release promoted through this pipeline.
+The Kubernetes release images are following the same path (kubernetes/release#4551, kubernetes/release#2616).
+The mechanism is documented in kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools#1972.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+The staging build signs build provenance for every release image and Helm chart.
+The provenance stays with each artifact when the artifact is promoted to the production registry.
+Consumers check the provenance against a documented Kueue build identity before they deploy Kueue.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter (`kpromo`, from kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools).
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+
+For SLSA, Sigstore, cosign, Fulcio, Rekor and OCI referrer, see [Appendix: External terms](#appendix-external-terms).
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built a released Kueue image
+
+An admin wants to verify the build provenance of a released Kueue image and confirm which commit built it.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate.
+Use the multi-arch image index digest, not a platform manifest digest.
+This story applies to released (tagged) versions, where the predicate records the tag ref.
+For images built from `main` or `release-*` branches, the predicate records the branch ref; use the commit SHA from `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` to identify the exact build.
+Resolve the release tag to its multi-arch index digest with `crane` (part of `go-containerregistry`):
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue:v<version>
+# sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+Use the output digest as `<multi-arch-index-digest>` in the commands below.
+During Alpha, only staging images carry attestations; replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/kueue` in the `crane` and `cosign` commands below.
+From Beta onward, production images carry attestations and the command applies as written.
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This excerpt shows only the source commit and builder fields relevant to commit verification.
+After `cosign verify-attestation` succeeds, compare `externalParameters.source.uri` with the expected tag (`git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>`) and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` with the known commit SHA for that release.
+A mismatch means the attestation was signed for a different build; reject it and do not treat the image as verified.
+The full predicate shape, including `buildType`, `resolvedDependencies`, and invocation ID, is described in [Provenance content](#provenance-content).
+
+The attestation is stored as an OCI referrer attached to the image digest — not inside the image itself.
+`cosign verify-attestation` (shown above) outputs a JSON object per attestation; the predicate is base64-encoded in `.payload`.
+To extract and pretty-print it:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  <image>@sha256:<digest> \
+  | jq -r '.payload' | base64 -d | jq .
+```
+
+To inspect the attestation without verifying the signature, use `cosign download attestation <image>@sha256:<digest>`.
+In the Artifact Registry console, navigate to the image digest and open the **Attestations** tab to browse attached referrers.
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+Staging artifacts have a 90-day retention policy.
+Attestations for Alpha builds are only verifiable in the staging registry within that window.
+After 90 days, the attestation is no longer available in staging; from Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+It needs Policy Controller v0.13.0 or later, the first release that supports `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+Earlier releases do not understand `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+If the field is silently dropped, the Policy Controller falls back to its default (legacy-format) verification;
+because Kueue produces only bundle-format attestations, the legacy check finds none and rejects the image.
+If `kubectl apply` rejects the manifest outright, the policy is never created and no enforcement applies.
+The `cosign verify-attestation` commands in Stories 1 and 3 need cosign v3.0.1 or later (v3.0.0 was tagged but never released), which reads bundle-format attestations by default.
+With cosign v2.5.0 to v2.6.x, add `--new-bundle-format`.
+Earlier releases cannot verify bundle-format image attestations: cosign v2.4.0 added bundle support only for blob commands such as `verify-blob-attestation`, not for `verify-attestation` on images.
+The Policy Controller admits Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present.
+When attestation verification fails — no matching provenance, wrong identity, or invalid signature — Policy Controller denies admission and returns a policy violation to the caller.
+This policy applies from Beta onward.
+During Alpha, replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/**` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/**` in the policy below:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      signatureFormat: bundle
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
+```
+
+Once CycloneDX SBOMs are published as OCI referrers (see [Future work ideas](#future-work-ideas)),
+the policy can be extended with an SBOM attestation entry alongside the provenance entry:
+
+```yaml
+        - name: sbom
+          predicateType: https://cyclonedx.org/bom
+```
+
+Requiring both build provenance and an SBOM blocks admission of any image that lacks either artifact.
+
+Alternatively, consumers running cluster-wide admission policies that cover multiple
+`registry.k8s.io` projects may prefer to verify against the SLSA verification summary
+that kpromo publishes for every promoted digest.
+It is signed by a single identity, `promoter-summaries@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`,
+shared across all `registry.k8s.io` projects.
+See [Verification summaries](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools/blob/main/docs/image-promotion.md#verification-summaries).
+
+#### Story 3: An admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue Helm chart they install
+
+An admin installs Kueue from the Helm chart at `oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue`.
+Before installing, they want to confirm which commit built the chart.
+`helm pull` on OCI charts requires Helm 3.8.0 or later; earlier versions use experimental OCI commands and are not supported.
+The predicate has the same shape as in Story 1, with the chart digest as the attestation subject.
+
+##### Alpha: verify the staging chart
+
+During Alpha, only the staging chart carries an attestation.
+
+First resolve the digest, then verify the attestation:
+
+```bash
+crane digest us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+Confirm the staging chart has been promoted to the production registry by checking that the
+digests match:
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<same-digest>
+```
+
+Only install the chart if both digests are identical.
+Install by digest, so the installed chart is the one verified above:
+
+```bash
+helm install kueue oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+##### Beta onward: verify the production chart
+
+From Beta, the attestation is attached to the production chart directly.
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+A chart attestation does not cover the images that the chart deploys; verify those separately, as in Story 1.
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+  The image promoter promotes the index digest, and `cosign verify-attestation` resolves
+  attestations from the index, so index-only attestation is sufficient for the Kueue
+  verification path.
+  kpromo rule #1998 states: "An index satisfies a provenance policy with its own provenance
+  OR when all its platform manifests do."
+  Kueue's policy is evaluated against the index digest, so index provenance alone satisfies it.
+  (Re-verify this rule against the kpromo version deployed at Beta, as the rule number and wording may change with kpromo releases.)
+  This differs from projects (such as Kubernetes releases) whose build attests both the
+  index and every per-arch manifest; Kueue has no requirement for per-arch attestations.
+  Per-arch manifests that are not individually attested receive `SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED`
+  verification summaries from kpromo.
+
+- During Alpha, attestations are attached to staging artifacts only.
+  Production-registry (`registry.k8s.io`) images do not carry attestations until the promoter policy change in `kubernetes/k8s.io` lands (Beta).
+- Staging artifacts are retained for 90 days by the staging project's Artifact Registry cleanup policy.
+  Attestations for Alpha releases are only verifiable in staging within that window.
+  From Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Under `warn`, the promoter does not reject an unattested artifact automatically.
+The release manager still holds the promoter manifest pull request until the attestation is present and verified, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+For an extended outage, set `SIGN=false` in the build to skip all signing and attestation.
+The build completes and the images are pushed without attestations.
+Under `warn` mode the promoter still promotes; the release manager must note the missing attestation in the promoter manifest pull request and verify once Sigstore recovers.
```

+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+The Security Profiles Operator (SPO) is the Kubernetes ecosystem pilot for this pattern.
+SPO uses Cloud Build with a project-specific staging service account, self-signed SLSA L1 provenance, and a kpromo provenance policy in `require` mode.
+SPO v1.1.2 was the first release promoted through this pipeline.
+The Kubernetes release images are following the same path (kubernetes/release#4551, kubernetes/release#2616).
+The mechanism is documented in kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools#1972.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+The staging build signs build provenance for every release image and Helm chart.
+The provenance stays with each artifact when the artifact is promoted to the production registry.
+Consumers check the provenance against a documented Kueue build identity before they deploy Kueue.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter (`kpromo`, from kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools).
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+
+For SLSA, Sigstore, cosign, Fulcio, Rekor and OCI referrer, see [Appendix: External terms](#appendix-external-terms).
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built a released Kueue image
+
+An admin wants to verify the build provenance of a released Kueue image and confirm which commit built it.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate.
+Use the multi-arch image index digest, not a platform manifest digest.
+This story applies to released (tagged) versions, where the predicate records the tag ref.
+For images built from `main` or `release-*` branches, the predicate records the branch ref; use the commit SHA from `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` to identify the exact build.
+Resolve the release tag to its multi-arch index digest with `crane` (part of `go-containerregistry`):
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue:v<version>
+# sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+Use the output digest as `<multi-arch-index-digest>` in the commands below.
+During Alpha, only staging images carry attestations; replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/kueue` in the `crane` and `cosign` commands below.
+From Beta onward, production images carry attestations and the command applies as written.
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This excerpt shows only the source commit and builder fields relevant to commit verification.
+After `cosign verify-attestation` succeeds, compare `externalParameters.source.uri` with the expected tag (`git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>`) and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` with the known commit SHA for that release.
+A mismatch means the attestation was signed for a different build; reject it and do not treat the image as verified.
+The full predicate shape, including `buildType`, `resolvedDependencies`, and invocation ID, is described in [Provenance content](#provenance-content).
+
+The attestation is stored as an OCI referrer attached to the image digest — not inside the image itself.
+`cosign verify-attestation` (shown above) outputs a JSON object per attestation; the predicate is base64-encoded in `.payload`.
+To extract and pretty-print it:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  <image>@sha256:<digest> \
+  | jq -r '.payload' | base64 -d | jq .
+```
+
+To inspect the attestation without verifying the signature, use `cosign download attestation <image>@sha256:<digest>`.
+In the Artifact Registry console, navigate to the image digest and open the **Attestations** tab to browse attached referrers.
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+Staging artifacts have a 90-day retention policy.
+Attestations for Alpha builds are only verifiable in the staging registry within that window.
+After 90 days, the attestation is no longer available in staging; from Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+It needs Policy Controller v0.13.0 or later, the first release that supports `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+Earlier releases do not understand `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+If the field is silently dropped, the Policy Controller falls back to its default (legacy-format) verification;
+because Kueue produces only bundle-format attestations, the legacy check finds none and rejects the image.
+If `kubectl apply` rejects the manifest outright, the policy is never created and no enforcement applies.
+The `cosign verify-attestation` commands in Stories 1 and 3 need cosign v3.0.1 or later (v3.0.0 was tagged but never released), which reads bundle-format attestations by default.
+With cosign v2.5.0 to v2.6.x, add `--new-bundle-format`.
+Earlier releases cannot verify bundle-format image attestations: cosign v2.4.0 added bundle support only for blob commands such as `verify-blob-attestation`, not for `verify-attestation` on images.
+The Policy Controller admits Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present.
+When attestation verification fails — no matching provenance, wrong identity, or invalid signature — Policy Controller denies admission and returns a policy violation to the caller.
+This policy applies from Beta onward.
+During Alpha, replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/**` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/**` in the policy below:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      signatureFormat: bundle
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
+```
+
+Once CycloneDX SBOMs are published as OCI referrers (see [Future work ideas](#future-work-ideas)),
+the policy can be extended with an SBOM attestation entry alongside the provenance entry:
+
+```yaml
+        - name: sbom
+          predicateType: https://cyclonedx.org/bom
+```
+
+Requiring both build provenance and an SBOM blocks admission of any image that lacks either artifact.
+
+Alternatively, consumers running cluster-wide admission policies that cover multiple
+`registry.k8s.io` projects may prefer to verify against the SLSA verification summary
+that kpromo publishes for every promoted digest.
+It is signed by a single identity, `promoter-summaries@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`,
+shared across all `registry.k8s.io` projects.
+See [Verification summaries](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools/blob/main/docs/image-promotion.md#verification-summaries).
+
+#### Story 3: An admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue Helm chart they install
+
+An admin installs Kueue from the Helm chart at `oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue`.
+Before installing, they want to confirm which commit built the chart.
+`helm pull` on OCI charts requires Helm 3.8.0 or later; earlier versions use experimental OCI commands and are not supported.
+The predicate has the same shape as in Story 1, with the chart digest as the attestation subject.
+
+##### Alpha: verify the staging chart
+
+During Alpha, only the staging chart carries an attestation.
+
+First resolve the digest, then verify the attestation:
+
+```bash
+crane digest us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+Confirm the staging chart has been promoted to the production registry by checking that the
+digests match:
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<same-digest>
+```
+
+Only install the chart if both digests are identical.
+Install by digest, so the installed chart is the one verified above:
+
+```bash
+helm install kueue oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+##### Beta onward: verify the production chart
+
+From Beta, the attestation is attached to the production chart directly.
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+A chart attestation does not cover the images that the chart deploys; verify those separately, as in Story 1.
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+  The image promoter promotes the index digest, and `cosign verify-attestation` resolves
+  attestations from the index, so index-only attestation is sufficient for the Kueue
+  verification path.
+  kpromo rule #1998 states: "An index satisfies a provenance policy with its own provenance
+  OR when all its platform manifests do."
+  Kueue's policy is evaluated against the index digest, so index provenance alone satisfies it.
+  (Re-verify this rule against the kpromo version deployed at Beta, as the rule number and wording may change with kpromo releases.)
+  This differs from projects (such as Kubernetes releases) whose build attests both the
+  index and every per-arch manifest; Kueue has no requirement for per-arch attestations.
+  Per-arch manifests that are not individually attested receive `SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED`
+  verification summaries from kpromo.
+
+- During Alpha, attestations are attached to staging artifacts only.
+  Production-registry (`registry.k8s.io`) images do not carry attestations until the promoter policy change in `kubernetes/k8s.io` lands (Beta).
+- Staging artifacts are retained for 90 days by the staging project's Artifact Registry cleanup policy.
+  Attestations for Alpha releases are only verifiable in staging within that window.
+  From Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Under `warn`, the promoter does not reject an unattested artifact automatically.
+The release manager still holds the promoter manifest pull request until the attestation is present and verified, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+For an extended outage, set `SIGN=false` in the build to skip all signing and attestation.
+The build completes and the images are pushed without attestations.
+Under `warn` mode the promoter still promotes; the release manager must note the missing attestation in the promoter manifest pull request and verify once Sigstore recovers.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check fails the build visibly if attestation fails.
+The release manager must still verify the attestation of each digest recorded in the promoter manifest pull request before it merges, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After each image and chart push, the build takes the pushed digest from the push output,
+   not from a later tag lookup. A tag can move between the push and a lookup, for example when
+   a concurrent build pushes the same tag, so a tag lookup could attest a different artifact.
+   Concurrent image builds record their digests separately. The tag is used only as the
+   push target.
+2. The build writes a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository URI, the git ref
+   that triggered the build, the git commit SHA, the builder identity, and the Cloud Build
+   invocation ID. For tag builds, the ref identifies the commit. For `main` and `release-*`
+   branch builds, the ref is the branch name and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit`
+   identifies the build.
+3. A pinned cosign version attaches the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer to
+   `artifact@sha256:<digest>` from Step 1, signed with the build service account's workload
+   identity.
+4. The build verifies the attestation on the same digest against the build identity as a
+   self-check, and fails if verification fails.
+
+The exact commands are defined in the implementation PR and documented in `RELEASE.md`.
+
+Setting `SIGN=false` skips all signing and attestation steps; the build completes and pushes images without any attestations.
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build.
+Per SLSA v1, `runDetails.builder.id` identifies the entity that produces and signs the predicate.
+The build writes and signs its own provenance, so the builder is the repository's Cloud Build configuration running as the `kueue-sa` service account — not the Prow job that submitted the build.
+SPO and the promo-tools provenance policy documentation use this form:
+`https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/<project>/serviceAccounts/<sa>/cloudbuild.yaml`
+For Kueue: `https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml`
+This value is also what the policy's `builders[].id` field must match (see [Changes in other repositories](#changes-in-other-repositories)).
+
+**Note:** The `buildType` URI is pinned to the specific commit being built (`$COMMIT_SHA` from Cloud Build), so it resolves to the `RELEASE.md` at that exact revision and cannot be changed after the attestation is signed. The `Staging artifact provenance v1` section must exist in `RELEASE.md` at the commit being attested — it is added as a prerequisite before enabling the attestation step (see [Alpha](#alpha)).
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "buildType": "https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/<commit>/RELEASE.md#staging-artifact-provenance-v1",
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    },
+    "internalParameters": {
+      "buildConfigSource": "cloudbuild.yaml"
+    },
+    "resolvedDependencies": [
+      { "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue", "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" } }
+    ]
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" },
+    "metadata": { "invocationId": "https://console.cloud.google.com/cloud-build/builds/<build-id>?project=<project-number>" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+`externalParameters.source` records the user-supplied tagged input (the git ref); `resolvedDependencies` records the resolved, pinned dependency (the specific commit). Both reference the same underlying commit SHA for a tag build.
+
+### Failure handling
+
+A failed attestation or self-check step fails the build with a non-zero exit code.
+If Step 3 (attachment) fails, the artifact has no attestation in the staging registry.
+If Step 4 (self-check) fails, the attestation is present but unverified; the release manager must treat it as unusable and must not promote that digest.
+In either case, rerunning the postsubmit signs the artifact again.
+The earlier push stays in the registry.
+The release promotion script resolves each release tag to a digest once, and records that digest in the promoter manifest pull request.
+`kpromo` promotes exactly the recorded digests; it does not resolve tags again.
+If the tag still points to the unattested push when the script runs, that unattested digest is promoted.
+Under `warn` mode, kpromo writes a FAILED verification summary line for each artifact that does not satisfy the policy; promotion still completes.
+kpromo also publishes a signed verification summary as an OCI referrer on `registry.k8s.io`, signed by the `promoter-summaries@k8s-releng-prod` service account.
+This summary records the verified SLSA level for every promoted artifact and is the authoritative record of what the promoter checked.
+The release manager must review the summary and confirm that every FAILED line is expected (for example, an artifact from before the attestation pipeline was enabled) before the promoter manifest pull request merges.
+The release manager must also:
+
+1. Wait until the rerun postsubmit, including its self-check, completes before running the release promotion script.
+2. Before opening the promoter manifest pull request, run `cosign verify-attestation` on every staging digest that will be recorded in it, as `<staging-artifact>@sha256:<digest>`, not on the tag.
+   This pre-promotion verification step confirms each attestation is valid before the digest is committed to the manifest.
+   Promotion then uses the same digest that was verified, so moving the tag after verification cannot change what is promoted.
+
+Under `require` mode, the promoter enforces this automatically: it rejects a digest that has no valid attestation.
+
+A digest's verification summary records the result of its first promotion — a `FAILED` summary is permanent for that digest.
+Kueue digests already carry `SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED` summaries on `registry.k8s.io`; a `FAILED` summary from an unattested promotion would be visible alongside them.
+To avoid a permanent `FAILED` record, add the promoter policy only after staging attestations are in place and verified.
+
+### Promotion
+
+kpromo v4.7.0 added per-project provenance policies and OCI referrer carry for container images.
+kpromo v4.8.0, deployed in the production promotion pipeline at the time this KEP was written, extends carry to Helm OCI charts.
+kpromo verifies the build attestation when present and carries it to the production registry as an OCI referrer.
+Carrying the attestation also requires the Kueue provenance policy in the promoter manifest in kubernetes/k8s.io (see [Changes in other repositories](#changes-in-other-repositories)). That change has not landed yet.
+The promotion signature is added after the copy and is unaffected.
+The promoter policy for Kueue starts in `warn` mode.
+After the first passing promotion under `warn`, the policy moves to `require`.
+
+### Release candidates
```

+# KEP-1466: SLSA build provenance for Kueue release artifacts
+
+<!-- toc -->

+- [Design Details](#design-details)

+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+The Security Profiles Operator (SPO) is the Kubernetes ecosystem pilot for this pattern.
+SPO uses Cloud Build with a project-specific staging service account, self-signed SLSA L1 provenance, and a kpromo provenance policy in `require` mode.
+SPO v1.1.2 was the first release promoted through this pipeline.
+The Kubernetes release images are following the same path (kubernetes/release#4551, kubernetes/release#2616).
+The mechanism is documented in kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools#1972.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+The staging build signs build provenance for every release image and Helm chart.
+The provenance stays with each artifact when the artifact is promoted to the production registry.
+Consumers check the provenance against a documented Kueue build identity before they deploy Kueue.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter (`kpromo`, from kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools).
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+
+For SLSA, Sigstore, cosign, Fulcio, Rekor and OCI referrer, see [Appendix: External terms](#appendix-external-terms).
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built a released Kueue image
+
+An admin wants to verify the build provenance of a released Kueue image and confirm which commit built it.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate.
+Use the multi-arch image index digest, not a platform manifest digest.
+This story applies to released (tagged) versions, where the predicate records the tag ref.
+For images built from `main` or `release-*` branches, the predicate records the branch ref; use the commit SHA from `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` to identify the exact build.
+Resolve the release tag to its multi-arch index digest with `crane` (part of `go-containerregistry`):
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue:v<version>
+# sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+Use the output digest as `<multi-arch-index-digest>` in the commands below.
+During Alpha, only staging images carry attestations; replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/kueue` in the `crane` and `cosign` commands below.
+From Beta onward, production images carry attestations and the command applies as written.
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This excerpt shows only the source commit and builder fields relevant to commit verification.
+After `cosign verify-attestation` succeeds, compare `externalParameters.source.uri` with the expected tag (`git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>`) and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` with the known commit SHA for that release.
+A mismatch means the attestation was signed for a different build; reject it and do not treat the image as verified.
+The full predicate shape, including `buildType`, `resolvedDependencies`, and invocation ID, is described in [Provenance content](#provenance-content).
+
+The attestation is stored as an OCI referrer attached to the image digest — not inside the image itself.
+`cosign verify-attestation` (shown above) outputs a JSON object per attestation; the predicate is base64-encoded in `.payload`.
+To extract and pretty-print it:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  <image>@sha256:<digest> \
+  | jq -r '.payload' | base64 -d | jq '.predicate'
+```
+
+To inspect the attestation without verifying the signature, use `cosign download attestation <image>@sha256:<digest>`.
+In the Artifact Registry console, navigate to the image digest and open the **Attestations** tab to browse attached referrers.
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+Staging artifacts have a 90-day retention policy.
+Attestations for Alpha builds are only verifiable in the staging registry within that window.
+After 90 days, the attestation is no longer available in staging; from Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+It needs Policy Controller v0.13.0 or later, the first release that supports `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+Earlier releases do not understand `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+If the field is silently dropped, the Policy Controller falls back to its default (legacy-format) verification;
+because Kueue produces only bundle-format attestations, the legacy check finds none and rejects the image.
+If `kubectl apply` rejects the manifest outright, the policy is never created and no enforcement applies.
+The `cosign verify-attestation` commands in Stories 1 and 3 need cosign v3.0.1 or later (v3.0.0 was tagged but never released), which reads bundle-format attestations by default.
+With cosign v2.5.0 to v2.6.x, add `--new-bundle-format`.
+Earlier releases cannot verify bundle-format image attestations: cosign v2.4.0 added bundle support only for blob commands such as `verify-blob-attestation`, not for `verify-attestation` on images.
+The Policy Controller admits Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present.
+When attestation verification fails — no matching provenance, wrong identity, or invalid signature — Policy Controller denies admission and returns a policy violation to the caller.
+This policy applies from Beta onward.
+During Alpha, replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/**` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/**` in the policy below:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      signatureFormat: bundle
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
+```
+
+Once CycloneDX SBOMs are published as OCI referrers (see [Future work ideas](#future-work-ideas)),
+the policy can be extended with an SBOM attestation entry alongside the provenance entry:
+
+```yaml
+        - name: sbom
+          predicateType: https://cyclonedx.org/bom
+```
+
+Requiring both build provenance and an SBOM blocks admission of any image that lacks either artifact.
+
+Alternatively, consumers running cluster-wide admission policies that cover multiple
+`registry.k8s.io` projects may prefer to verify against the SLSA verification summary
+that kpromo publishes for every promoted digest.
+It is signed by a single identity, `promoter-summaries@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`,
+shared across all `registry.k8s.io` projects.
+See [Verification summaries](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools/blob/main/docs/image-promotion.md#verification-summaries).
+
+#### Story 3: An admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue Helm chart they install
+
+An admin installs Kueue from the Helm chart at `oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue`.
+Before installing, they want to confirm which commit built the chart.
+`helm pull` on OCI charts requires Helm 3.8.0 or later; earlier versions use experimental OCI commands and are not supported.
+The predicate has the same shape as in Story 1, with the chart digest as the attestation subject.
+
+##### Alpha: verify the staging chart
+
+During Alpha, only the staging chart carries an attestation.
+
+First resolve the digest, then verify the attestation:
+
+```bash
+crane digest us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+Confirm the staging chart has been promoted to the production registry by checking that the
+digests match:
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<same-digest>
+```
+
+Only install the chart if both digests are identical.
+Install by digest, so the installed chart is the one verified above:
+
+```bash
+helm install kueue oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+##### Beta onward: verify the production chart
+
+From Beta, the attestation is attached to the production chart directly.
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+A chart attestation does not cover the images that the chart deploys; verify those separately, as in Story 1.
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+  The image promoter promotes the index digest, and `cosign verify-attestation` resolves
+  attestations from the index, so index-only attestation is sufficient for the Kueue
+  verification path.
+  kpromo rule #1998 states: "An index satisfies a provenance policy with its own provenance
+  OR when all its platform manifests do."
+  Kueue's policy is evaluated against the index digest, so index provenance alone satisfies it.
+  (Re-verify this rule against the kpromo version deployed at Beta, as the rule number and wording may change with kpromo releases.)
+  This differs from projects (such as Kubernetes releases) whose build attests both the
+  index and every per-arch manifest; Kueue has no requirement for per-arch attestations.
+  Per-arch manifests that are not individually attested receive `SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED`
+  verification summaries from kpromo.
+
+- During Alpha, attestations are attached to staging artifacts only.
+  Production-registry (`registry.k8s.io`) images do not carry attestations until the promoter policy change in `kubernetes/k8s.io` lands (Beta).
+- Staging artifacts are retained for 90 days by the staging project's Artifact Registry cleanup policy.
+  Attestations for Alpha releases are only verifiable in staging within that window.
+  From Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Under `warn`, the promoter does not reject an unattested artifact automatically.
+The release manager still holds the promoter manifest pull request until the attestation is present and verified, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+For an extended outage, set `SIGN=false` in the build to skip all signing and attestation.
+The build completes and the images are pushed without attestations.
+Under `warn` mode, the release manager must still run `cosign verify-attestation` on each staging digest before opening the promoter manifest pull request, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+A digest with no valid attestation must not be recorded in the manifest during the outage.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check fails the build visibly if attestation fails.
+The release manager must still verify the attestation of each digest recorded in the promoter manifest pull request before it merges, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After each image and chart push, the build takes the pushed digest from the push output,
+   not from a later tag lookup. A tag can move between the push and a lookup, for example when
+   a concurrent build pushes the same tag, so a tag lookup could attest a different artifact.
+   Concurrent image builds record their digests separately. The tag is used only as the
+   push target.
+2. The build writes a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository URI, the git ref
+   that triggered the build, the git commit SHA, the builder identity, and the Cloud Build
+   invocation ID. For tag builds, the ref identifies the commit. For `main` and `release-*`
+   branch builds, the ref is the branch name and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit`
+   identifies the build.
+3. A pinned cosign version attaches the predicate as a Sigstore bundle OCI referrer to
+   `artifact@sha256:<digest>` from Step 1, signed with the build service account's workload
+   identity.
+4. The build verifies the attestation on the same digest against the build identity as a
+   self-check, and fails if verification fails.
+
+The exact commands are defined in the implementation PR and documented in `RELEASE.md`.
+
+Setting `SIGN=false` skips all signing and attestation steps; the build completes and pushes images without any attestations.
+A local dry-run mode writes the predicate without signing.
+
+### Provenance content
+
+The predicate has this shape. Values in angle brackets vary per build.
+Per SLSA v1, `runDetails.builder.id` identifies the entity that produces and signs the predicate.
+The build writes and signs its own provenance, so the builder is the repository's Cloud Build configuration running as the `kueue-sa` service account — not the Prow job that submitted the build.
+SPO and the promo-tools provenance policy documentation use this form:
+`https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/<project>/serviceAccounts/<sa>/cloudbuild.yaml`
+For Kueue: `https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml`
+This value is also what the policy's `builders[].id` field must match (see [Changes in other repositories](#changes-in-other-repositories)).
+
+**Note:** The `buildType` URI is pinned to the specific commit being built (`$COMMIT_SHA` from Cloud Build), so it resolves to the `RELEASE.md` at that exact revision and cannot be changed after the attestation is signed. The `Staging artifact provenance v1` section must exist in `RELEASE.md` at the commit being attested — it is added as a prerequisite before enabling the attestation step (see [Alpha](#alpha)).
```

  The build is started with `gcloud builds submit` by the Prow image-builder, not by a Cloud Build trigger. As far as I know, `$COMMIT_SHA` is set only for triggered builds, so it will be empty here. The Attestation step already takes the commit from `git rev-parse HEAD`. Can we use the same value here?
  
  ```suggestion
  **Note:** The `buildType` URI is pinned to the commit SHA recorded in `gitCommit` (from `git rev-parse HEAD`), so it resolves to the `RELEASE.md` at that exact revision and cannot be changed after the attestation is signed.
  ```

+
+## Summary
+
+This KEP adds signed SLSA v1 build provenance to Kueue's staging images and Helm charts.
+Consumers can then verify which source commit and build produced the artifacts promoted to the production registry.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Staging artifacts carry no build provenance today.
+Promoted images carry a promotion signature, but no record of the build that produced them.
+A promotion signature answers "was this artifact promoted through the official pipeline?".
+It does not answer "which commit built it?".
+The image promoter can carry build provenance to the production registry, but only when the staging artifact already carries it.
+Release consumers (cluster admins, platform teams, and security auditors) cannot verify the build origin of Kueue images.
+
+The Security Profiles Operator (SPO) is the Kubernetes ecosystem pilot for this pattern.
+SPO uses Cloud Build with a project-specific staging service account, self-signed SLSA L1 provenance, and a kpromo provenance policy in `require` mode.
+SPO v1.1.2 was the first release promoted through this pipeline.
+The Kubernetes release images are following the same path (kubernetes/release#4551, kubernetes/release#2616).
+The mechanism is documented in kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools#1972.
+
+### Goals
+
+- Every promoted image and Helm chart carries a Sigstore-signed SLSA v1 build provenance attestation on staging.
+- The attestation survives promotion to the production registry.
+- Release candidates are covered by the same mechanism.
+- Consumers can verify provenance with a documented signing identity and issuer.
+- A failed attestation step fails the build visibly.
+
+### Non-Goals
+
+- Provenance for GitHub release assets (`kubectl-kueue` binaries, rendered manifests, raw Helm chart tarballs). These are future work.
+- SLSA Build Level 2 or higher.
+- Changes to Kueue's Kubernetes APIs, configuration, or controller behavior.
+- Attesting images that are not promoted to the production registry, such as periodic build images.
+- Retroactive attestation of past releases.
+
+## Proposal
+
+The staging build signs build provenance for every release image and Helm chart.
+The provenance stays with each artifact when the artifact is promoted to the production registry.
+Consumers check the provenance against a documented Kueue build identity before they deploy Kueue.
+
+### Terminology
+
+- **Staging artifact**: an image or Helm chart published to the staging Artifact Registry by a postsubmit build.
+- **Promoted artifact**: a staging artifact copied to the production registry by the image promoter (`kpromo`, from kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools).
+- **Build provenance**: a signed statement of which source, build system, and invocation produced an artifact.
+- **Promotion signature**: a signature added by the image promoter at copy time. It attests the copy, not the build.
+- **Build identity** (`kueue-sa`): the service account that runs the staging build. Its email address is the Sigstore signing identity.
+
+For SLSA, Sigstore, cosign, Fulcio, Rekor and OCI referrer, see [Appendix: External terms](#appendix-external-terms).
+
+### User Stories
+
+#### Story 1: A cluster admin cannot tell which commit built a released Kueue image
+
+An admin wants to verify the build provenance of a released Kueue image and confirm which commit built it.
+They verify the attestation of the image digest and read the source commit from the predicate.
+Use the multi-arch image index digest, not a platform manifest digest.
+This story applies to released (tagged) versions, where the predicate records the tag ref.
+For images built from `main` or `release-*` branches, the predicate records the branch ref; use the commit SHA from `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` to identify the exact build.
+Resolve the release tag to its multi-arch index digest with `crane` (part of `go-containerregistry`):
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue:v<version>
+# sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+Use the output digest as `<multi-arch-index-digest>` in the commands below.
+During Alpha, only staging images carry attestations; replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/kueue` in the `crane` and `cosign` commands below.
+From Beta onward, production images carry attestations and the command applies as written.
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/kueue@sha256:<multi-arch-index-digest>
+```
+
+The predicate records the source and the commit:
+
+```json
+{
+  "buildDefinition": {
+    "externalParameters": {
+      "source": {
+        "uri": "git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>",
+        "digest": { "gitCommit": "<commit-sha>" }
+      }
+    }
+  },
+  "runDetails": {
+    "builder": { "id": "https://cloudbuild.googleapis.com/projects/k8s-staging-images/serviceAccounts/kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com/cloudbuild.yaml" }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+This excerpt shows only the source commit and builder fields relevant to commit verification.
+After `cosign verify-attestation` succeeds, compare `externalParameters.source.uri` with the expected tag (`git+https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue@refs/tags/v<version>`) and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit` with the known commit SHA for that release.
+A mismatch means the attestation was signed for a different build; reject it and do not treat the image as verified.
+The full predicate shape, including `buildType`, `resolvedDependencies`, and invocation ID, is described in [Provenance content](#provenance-content).
+
+The attestation is stored as an OCI referrer attached to the image digest — not inside the image itself.
+`cosign verify-attestation` (shown above) outputs a JSON object per attestation; the predicate is base64-encoded in `.payload`.
+To extract and pretty-print it:
+
+```bash
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com \
+  <image>@sha256:<digest> \
+  | jq -r '.payload' | base64 -d | jq '.predicate'
+```
+
+To inspect the attestation without verifying the signature, use `cosign download attestation <image>@sha256:<digest>`.
+In the Artifact Registry console, navigate to the image digest and open the **Attestations** tab to browse attached referrers.
+
+If no attestation is present — because the image predates the feature or the build failed before the attestation step — `cosign` exits with a non-zero status and prints a message such as `no matching attestations`. This is expected for any Kueue image built before the Alpha milestone or during an interrupted build.
+
+Staging artifacts have a 90-day retention policy.
+Attestations for Alpha builds are only verifiable in the staging registry within that window.
+After 90 days, the attestation is no longer available in staging; from Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+#### Story 2: A platform team wants to reject Kueue images without build provenance at admission time
+
+A platform team runs the [Sigstore Policy Controller](https://docs.sigstore.dev/policy-controller/overview/) in their clusters.
+The `ClusterImagePolicy` below is a Policy Controller resource and has no effect without it.
+It needs Policy Controller v0.13.0 or later, the first release that supports `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+Earlier releases do not understand `signatureFormat: bundle`.
+If the field is silently dropped, the Policy Controller falls back to its default (legacy-format) verification;
+because Kueue produces only bundle-format attestations, the legacy check finds none and rejects the image.
+If `kubectl apply` rejects the manifest outright, the policy is never created and no enforcement applies.
+The `cosign verify-attestation` commands in Stories 1 and 3 need cosign v3.0.1 or later (v3.0.0 was tagged but never released), which reads bundle-format attestations by default.
+With cosign v2.5.0 to v2.6.x, add `--new-bundle-format`.
+Earlier releases cannot verify bundle-format image attestations: cosign v2.4.0 added bundle support only for blob commands such as `verify-blob-attestation`, not for `verify-attestation` on images.
+The Policy Controller admits Kueue images only when a provenance attestation from the Kueue build identity is present.
+When attestation verification fails — no matching provenance, wrong identity, or invalid signature — Policy Controller denies admission and returns a policy violation to the caller.
+This policy applies from Beta onward.
+During Alpha, replace `registry.k8s.io/kueue/**` with `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/**` in the policy below:
+
+```yaml
+apiVersion: policy.sigstore.dev/v1beta1
+kind: ClusterImagePolicy
+metadata:
+  name: kueue-provenance
+spec:
+  images:
+    - glob: "registry.k8s.io/kueue/**"
+  authorities:
+    - keyless:
+        identities:
+          - issuer: https://accounts.google.com
+            subject: kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com
+      signatureFormat: bundle
+      attestations:
+        - name: build-provenance
+          predicateType: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
+```
+
+Once CycloneDX SBOMs are published as OCI referrers (see [Future work ideas](#future-work-ideas)),
+the policy can be extended with an SBOM attestation entry alongside the provenance entry:
+
+```yaml
+        - name: sbom
+          predicateType: https://cyclonedx.org/bom
+```
+
+Requiring both build provenance and an SBOM blocks admission of any image that lacks either artifact.
+
+Alternatively, consumers running cluster-wide admission policies that cover multiple
+`registry.k8s.io` projects may prefer to verify against the SLSA verification summary
+that kpromo publishes for every promoted digest.
+It is signed by a single identity, `promoter-summaries@k8s-releng-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`,
+shared across all `registry.k8s.io` projects.
+See [Verification summaries](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/promo-tools/blob/main/docs/image-promotion.md#verification-summaries).
+
+#### Story 3: An admin cannot tell which commit built the Kueue Helm chart they install
+
+An admin installs Kueue from the Helm chart at `oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue`.
+Before installing, they want to confirm which commit built the chart.
+`helm pull` on OCI charts requires Helm 3.8.0 or later; earlier versions use experimental OCI commands and are not supported.
+The predicate has the same shape as in Story 1, with the chart digest as the attestation subject.
+
+##### Alpha: verify the staging chart
+
+During Alpha, only the staging chart carries an attestation.
+
+First resolve the digest, then verify the attestation:
+
+```bash
+crane digest us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/k8s-staging-images/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+Confirm the staging chart has been promoted to the production registry by checking that the
+digests match:
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<same-digest>
+```
+
+Only install the chart if both digests are identical.
+Install by digest, so the installed chart is the one verified above:
+
+```bash
+helm install kueue oci://registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+##### Beta onward: verify the production chart
+
+From Beta, the attestation is attached to the production chart directly.
+
+```bash
+crane digest registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue:<chart-version>
+# sha256:<digest>
+
+cosign verify-attestation \
+  --type slsaprovenance1 \
+  --certificate-identity kueue-sa@k8s-staging-images.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
+  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://accounts.google.com \
+  registry.k8s.io/kueue/charts/kueue@sha256:<digest>
+```
+
+A chart attestation does not cover the images that the chart deploys; verify those separately, as in Story 1.
+
+### Notes/Constraints/Caveats
+
+- The level achieved is SLSA Build L1.
+  The build writes its own provenance predicate, and build steps are not isolated from each other.
+- Attestations attach to the multi-arch index digest that the image promoter references.
+  Platform-specific manifests do not carry their own attestation.
+  The image promoter promotes the index digest, and `cosign verify-attestation` resolves
+  attestations from the index, so index-only attestation is sufficient for the Kueue
+  verification path.
+  kpromo rule #1998 states: "An index satisfies a provenance policy with its own provenance
+  OR when all its platform manifests do."
+  Kueue's policy is evaluated against the index digest, so index provenance alone satisfies it.
+  (Re-verify this rule against the kpromo version deployed at Beta, as the rule number and wording may change with kpromo releases.)
+  This differs from projects (such as Kubernetes releases) whose build attests both the
+  index and every per-arch manifest; Kueue has no requirement for per-arch attestations.
+  Per-arch manifests that are not individually attested receive `SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED`
+  verification summaries from kpromo.
+
+- During Alpha, attestations are attached to staging artifacts only.
+  Production-registry (`registry.k8s.io`) images do not carry attestations until the promoter policy change in `kubernetes/k8s.io` lands (Beta).
+- Staging artifacts are retained for 90 days by the staging project's Artifact Registry cleanup policy.
+  Attestations for Alpha releases are only verifiable in staging within that window.
+  From Beta onward, attestations are carried to the production registry and are not subject to this limit.
+
+### Risks and Mitigations
+
+#### A Sigstore outage can delay staging builds and releases
+
+A staging build cannot sign or verify while Sigstore is unavailable.
+Rerun the postsubmit after the outage.
+Under `warn`, the promoter does not reject an unattested artifact automatically.
+The release manager still holds the promoter manifest pull request until the attestation is present and verified, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+For an extended outage, set `SIGN=false` in the build to skip all signing and attestation.
+The build completes and the images are pushed without attestations.
+Under `warn` mode, the release manager must still run `cosign verify-attestation` on each staging digest before opening the promoter manifest pull request, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+A digest with no valid attestation must not be recorded in the manifest during the outage.
+
+#### Anyone who can act as the build identity can sign false provenance
+
+Access to the service account is limited to staging project administrators and the Cloud Build pipeline.
+Consumers must pin both the signing identity and the issuer when they verify.
+Consumers must not treat L1 provenance as tamper-proof.
+
+#### An unattested artifact can be promoted during the transition period
+
+The promoter policy starts in warn mode, so an unattested artifact can still be promoted.
+Until the policy requires provenance, the in-build self-check fails the build visibly if attestation fails.
+The release manager must still verify the attestation of each digest recorded in the promoter manifest pull request before it merges, as described in [Failure handling](#failure-handling).
+
+#### Consumers may assume L1 provenance gives stronger guarantees than it does
+
+The consumer documentation, tracked separately, states the SLSA level and its limits.
+
+## Design Details
+
+### Attested artifacts
+
+| Artifact | Type | Phase |
+|---|---|---|
+| kueue | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-backend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueueviz-frontend | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster | Image | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-populator chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| kueue-priority-booster chart | Helm chart | 1 (this KEP) |
+| Periodic build images (debug, importer, ray-mini) | Image | Not attested |
+| GitHub release assets | Binary and manifest | Future work |
+
+### Build identity
+
+The staging build runs as a dedicated service account, `kueue-sa`, in the staging project.
+The account already has Artifact Registry write access and OIDC token-creator permissions.
+The build obtains a Fulcio identity certificate from its ambient Google identity, so it needs no extra credentials.
+Consumers verify against the account's email address and the Google OIDC issuer.
+
+### Attestation step
+
+1. After each image and chart push, the build takes the pushed digest from the push output,
+   not from a later tag lookup. A tag can move between the push and a lookup, for example when
+   a concurrent build pushes the same tag, so a tag lookup could attest a different artifact.
+   Concurrent image builds record their digests separately. The tag is used only as the
+   push target.
+2. The build writes a SLSA v1 predicate that records the source repository URI, the git ref
+   that triggered the build, the git commit SHA, the builder identity, and the Cloud Build
+   invocation ID. For tag builds, the ref identifies the commit. For `main` and `release-*`
+   branch builds, the ref is the branch name and `externalParameters.source.digest.gitCommit`
+   identifies the build.
```

  Where does the build get the git ref? Today the only source is `_PULL_BASE_REF`, which Prow passes with `--env-passthrough=PULL_BASE_REF`. It holds a short name like `main`, `release-0.15` or `v0.15.0` (see the comment in `cloudbuild.yaml`). Story 1 and the predicate example expect a full ref, `refs/tags/v<version>`. Please name the source and say how the build turns the short name into a full ref. For example: a name that matches the semver regex of the Prow job becomes `refs/tags/<name>`, and any other name becomes `refs/heads/<name>`.
